chunks: I asked him about eating the meat of chicken in the villages, where they do not prevent them from anything — they pass over human excrement and are left free upon it — and about eating their eggs. So he said: There is no problem with it.

key_terms.الدَّسَاكِر: Villages, rural hamlets (singular: daskar) — settlements outside major cities
key_terms.الْجَلَّالَة: Dung-eater (jallalah) — an animal that habitually consumes impurities; implied context of this hadith
key_terms.الْعَذِرَة: Human excrement, feces — ritually impure substance
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem/harm — standard jurisprudential formula permitting an act
key_terms.مُخَلًّى: Left free, unrestricted — not confined or supervised

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat chicken that walks on impurities and their eggs in Islam?
ai.summary: A companion asks Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) about the permissibility of eating the meat and eggs of free-range chickens in rural villages that roam freely and consume impure substances including human waste. The Imam rules there is no harm in eating such chicken or their eggs. This ruling reflects the jurisprudential principle that minor or incidental contact with najasah does not render the animal's meat forbidden unless it has become a habitual dung-eater (jallalah), and in this case the questioner's framing emphasizes that the animals merely 'pass over' the excrement.
